root_idea.summary: The root chiefly concerns becoming perceptible through shining, flashing, or appearing.
root_idea.development: From the idea of gleaming or coming into view, the lexicon develops usages for visible signs, broad boards and bones, and alteration by heat that makes a surface visibly changed. Thirst and the air between heaven and earth are treated as divergent branches.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form لَوْح.
Displayed as the distinct Quranic feminine intensive form لَوَّاحَة.

senses.definition: A broad, thin board or plank.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, this is used for the planks of the vessel in 54:13. The form may also denote a comparable broad, flat object.

senses.definition: A tablet or writing surface, especially one bearing an inscription.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses the plural for the tablets on which the divine writing was given, and the singular for a Tablet. This sense includes a writing surface made of wood or a similar material.

senses.definition: The Preserved or Guarded Tablet, the repository associated with the record of divine decrees.
senses.usage_conditions: A specific Quranic expression, اللَّوْحُ المَحْفُوظُ. Its precise nature is not defined by the lexical evidence; traditional explanations associate it with the divine record or a repository of ordained events.
A Quranic descriptive use, with the skin of human beings as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shine, gleam, flash, or become apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of light, lightning, stars, a person coming forth, an affair becoming manifest, or hoariness appearing. The lightning usage can describe a slight flash or illumination of what surrounds it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To see, catch sight of, or look toward something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive construction means to see or behold; لَاحَ إِلَى can mean to look at or toward. One reported construction describes seeing something and then losing sight of it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To thirst, whether slightly or quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate verbal branch from the appearance-and-shining sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alter or waste someone, making him lean or lank; to scorch or blacken the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The altering causes cited include thirst, travel, cold, illness, and grief; heat, fire, or the sun may alter the skin's color and scorch it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To heat a thing with fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alter a person's condition or color, including making the hair white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence specifically records hoariness as the cause of whitening; the usage is distinct from merely heating an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be cautious or fearful of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction with مِنْ marking the thing feared or avoided.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To signal by waving or displaying an object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The signal may be made from a distance with a garment, sword, or another visible object; the related example describes signaling to a dog with bread.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away with, or take away, what belongs to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed construction concerning property or a rightful possession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To destroy someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or try to see into an affair or matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense is glossed by تَبَصَّرَ, examining or seeking insight into the matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A glance or quick look.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal visual sense, compared with a light or quick look.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shoulder blade or other broad bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The shoulder blade may be specified as the part on which writing is made; the word can also denote a wide bone generally or the remaining broad bones of an emaciated person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The air or atmosphere between heaven and earth, especially the upper air near the clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct vocalized noun, also called سُكَاك in the cited expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thirsty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used specifically in the expression إِبِلٌ لَوْحَى, thirsty camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shining, glistening, or intensely white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The terms can be used substantively for a wild bull or for daybreak, named for its whiteness; they also occur in an expression for the afternoon when the sun is white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The apparent or external parts of a thing, especially the signs that reveal it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of visible signs such as the apparent signs of hoariness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shining weapons, especially swords; alternatively, sword cases or receptacles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The shining-weapons interpretation relates to their whiteness. An alternative interpretation takes the expression as referring to board-made sword cases with their scabbards and fittings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large-boned or having large shoulder blades or other wide bones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a camel or a man; it can also describe an animal having especially large or excellent broad bones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use distinct from the physical descriptions of bone structure and leanness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean, lank, light of flesh, or slender in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people of either sex, to a beast of carriage that quickly becomes so, and to a woman who quickly becomes lean.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quickly becoming thirsty; of a wind, very thirsty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a beast that soon thirsts and in the expression رِيحٌ مِلْوَاحٌ, a very thirsty wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of decoy bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical use identified by cross-reference in the entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Altered by fire, the sun, travel, or similar exposure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an arrow before it receives feathers and a head when fire has altered it, and to an iron arrowhead or spearhead; it can also describe something altered by the sun or travel.

Covers the broad thin object and its broad-bone branch.

cautions: The precise nature of the Quranic Preserved Tablet is left unspecified by the lexical evidence; reported explanations identify it with a guarded record or repository of divine decrees.
